facts.text: The shipped model SDF gives the drone plugin's ROS node the namespace /simple_drone.
The plugin header declares the relative topic defaults cmd_vel, posctrl, imu, takeoff, land, reset and dronevel_mode.
The plugin header declares the relative topic defaults gt_pose, gt_vel, gt_acc, cmd_mode, state and odom.
The plugin header includes geometry_msgs/Twist and Pose, sensor_msgs/Imu, std_msgs/Empty, Bool, String and Int8, and nav_msgs/Odometry.
The plugin header defines LANDED_MODEL 0, FLYING_MODEL 1, TAKINGOFF_MODEL 2 and LANDING_MODEL 3.
InitSubscribers creates a geometry_msgs::msg::Twist subscription on the cmd_vel default with best-effort KeepLast(1) QoS.
InitSubscribers creates a std_msgs::msg::Bool subscription on the posctrl default.
InitSubscribers creates a std_msgs::msg::Empty subscription on the takeoff default.
InitSubscribers creates a std_msgs::msg::Empty subscription on the land default.
InitSubscribers creates a std_msgs::msg::Empty subscription on the reset default.
InitSubscribers creates a std_msgs::msg::Bool subscription on the dronevel_mode default.
InitPublishers creates a geometry_msgs::msg::Pose publisher on the gt_pose default with queue size 1024.
InitPublishers creates a geometry_msgs::msg::Twist publisher on the gt_vel default.
InitPublishers creates a geometry_msgs::msg::Twist publisher on the gt_acc default.
InitPublishers creates a std_msgs::msg::String publisher on the cmd_mode default.
InitPublishers creates a std_msgs::msg::Int8 publisher on the state default.
The plugin's ROS setup creates only these topic subscriptions and publications; no service or action server is created for flight control or stopping.
TakeoffCallback changes LANDED_MODEL to TAKINGOFF_MODEL and resets the command timer; it publishes no acknowledgement.
LandCallback changes FLYING_MODEL or TAKINGOFF_MODEL to LANDING_MODEL and resets the command timer; it publishes no acknowledgement.
ResetCallback logs and calls Reset(); it returns no response.

The private Reset() resets the roll, pitch, yaw and velocity x, y and z PID controllers, sets the link force and torque to zero and resets the cached pose, velocity, angular velocity, acceleration and euler; it does not assign navi_state, cmd_vel, m_posCtrl, m_velMode or the position PID controllers.
DroneSimpleController::Reset() only calls the private Reset().

UpdateDynamics computes the force and torque from the stored cmd_vel: its linear fields are position targets when m_posCtrl is set and navi_state is FLYING_MODEL; in normal control linear.z drives the vertical velocity controller and angular.z the yaw controller in every state.
UpdateDynamics adds no force or torque in LANDED_MODEL, the computed force and torque in FLYING_MODEL, 1.5 times them in TAKINGOFF_MODEL and 0.8 times them in LANDING_MODEL.
PosCtrlCallback stores the Bool data in m_posCtrl.
SwitchModeCallback stores the Bool data in m_velMode and publishes the String 'velocity' or 'position' on cmd_mode.
CmdCallback stores the full Twist and adds drift and small-noise offsets to angular x/y/z and linear z.
UpdateState changes TAKINGOFF_MODEL to FLYING_MODEL after 0.5 s and LANDING_MODEL to LANDED_MODEL after 1.0 s, then publishes the Int8 navi_state every update.
UpdateDynamics reads the Gazebo world pose and publishes that Pose on gt_pose.
UpdateDynamics publishes body_vel, computed as pose.Rot().RotateVector(velocity), as the linear part of a Twist on gt_vel.
UpdateDynamics publishes body_acc, computed as pose.Rot().RotateVector(acceleration), as the linear part of a Twist on gt_acc.
The Python helper publishes Empty, Bool and Twist messages on the private (~/) takeoff, land, reset, posctrl, cmd_vel and dronevel_mode topics.
The Python move helper documents linear velocity in m/s and angular velocity in rad/s.
The Python moveTo helper documents x, y and z as metres and publishes them in the cmd_vel Twist linear fields.
The README lists cmd_vel, land, takeoff, posctrl, dronevel_mode, cmd_mode, state and reset as the control topics, with their ROS message types.
The README lists gt_acc, gt_pose and gt_vel as the ground-truth topic contracts.
The shipped reset_sim.sh helper calls the /reset_world std_srvs/srv/Empty service.
The drone plugin connects its Update to the world-update begin event.
Update returns at once when no simulation time passed, and otherwise runs UpdateState and UpdateDynamics.
In position control, while flying, UpdateDynamics feeds the cmd_vel linear fields to the position controllers as targets.
The gazebo launch includes gazebo_ros's gzserver.launch.py with the drone world.
The bringup launch starts the teleop_joystick node or the keyboard teleop node in the model namespace.
The gazebo_ros init plugin's /reset_world handler resets the world's model entities.
gzserver.launch.py adds the init and factory gazebo_ros system plugins to the server command.
gzserver.launch.py defaults its init and factory arguments to true.
The init plugin takes the shared gazebo_ros node from gazebo_ros::Node::Get().
gazebo_ros::Node::Get creates the shared node named gazebo with an empty namespace.
The gazebo_ros executor spins its nodes on a thread of its own.
The init plugin creates the pause_physics and unpause_physics services with the std_srvs::srv::Empty type.
OnPause calls world_->SetPaused(true).
OnUnpause calls world_->SetPaused(false).
The init plugin publishes the simulation clock from a world-update-begin callback.
The factory plugin creates the get_model_list service with the gazebo_msgs::srv::GetModelList type.
GetModelList sets header.stamp to the world's simulation time, lists the model names and sets success true.
The GetModelList response documents header.stamp as the simulation time when the data was collected.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.

determinism.notes: scripted request/response transport with placeholder state values; no physics step, no wall-clock pacing and no trajectory replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free scripted contract fake (no Gazebo, no physics, no captured traffic)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free scripted transport: it answers the declared endpoints with placeholder messages and runs no Gazebo, plugin, PID controller, physics, sensor or rosbridge process
the preference in the task card is the upstream Gazebo simulator; it cannot be started here, so this package uses an F0 contract fake instead of the upstream simulator
the fake does not model takeoff, landing or flight dynamics; it only records the publication and updates a placeholder state label
the fake's state, pose, mode and message values are test data, not measurements and not captured traffic
the upstream plugin adds drift and small-noise offsets to cmd_vel; the fake does not
the camera, IMU, sonar, GPS and odometry topics of the upstream simulation are not exposed; NOT COVERED: the front and bottom sensor_msgs/Image streams

/reset_world (gazebo_ros's init plugin, a companion) resets the model entities, and the plugin's Reset() keeps navi_state and the stored cmd_vel, so a world reset is not a stop; the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause, confirmed by the E1 stall read-back: the fake keeps a paused flag that /pause_physics sets and a sim-time stamp that /get_model_list reports and that advances on every answer unless paused; it runs no Gazebo World::Step

a frozen get_model_list stamp is also what a hung but unpaused gzserver shows (nothing advances then either); a GUI step or a WorldControl multi_step between the two samples fails the check (fails closed); the e-stop declares estop_latency_ms 1500 because the pause (400 ms), two read-backs (300 ms each) and the 250 ms interval exceed the default 1000 ms budget

no unpause is offered: in position control the cmd_vel linear fields are position targets (plugin_drone_private.cpp:492-520), so a zero Twist is a flight to the world origin; a take-off in progress continues with 1.5 times the force (573-585, UpdateState 395-416); CmdCallback adds drift and small noise to every stored command (227-254); and the bringup's teleop publishes on the same topics (sjtu_drone_bringup.launch.py:27-48); the package cannot clear the stored motion first, so the operator recovers outside MHS (land or re-command the drone, then the Gazebo GUI play button or ros2 service call /unpause_physics)

while paused, state and gt_pose (published from the plugin's world update) and /clock are silent and those reads fail NOT_READY after their timeouts (the fake silences them while its flag is set); the commands still publish and the plugin stores them for the next unpause

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI, a WorldControl message or any ROS 2 client of /unpause_physics; MHS does not watch the sim time after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)

the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 3.9.0 (Humble) and 11.15.1 releases the companion citations name (the clone also builds on Iron and Rolling; this package is pinned to Humble); rosbridge cannot read their versions

the fake acknowledges /reset_world and records the reset publication without changing its state label or stored command, as the plugin's Reset() does; it does not model what the Gazebo world reset does to the model pose

the fake answers every cmd_mode and cmd_vel subscription at once with its last value; live, the plugin publishes cmd_mode only from SwitchModeCallback and cmd_vel carries only what clients publish, so those reads return only when a message arrives while they wait; the last_cmd_vel read is an explicit capability, not the device resource, so no command waits for it

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused: two get_model_list answers 250 ms apart carried the same sim time, so the drone plugin's update applies no force; it is a frozen sim time, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: an operator lands or re-commands the drone and unpauses outside MHS.
